# USD NURBS curve fixtures

This directory contains one unchanged Maya-exported layer and seven authored
curve/container controls. The authored inputs are generated by
`examples/fixtures/usd_nurbs.rs` and are MIT licensed with Catwalk. The Maya
layer keeps its separate Apache-2.0 license and source attribution. Regeneration
uses the checked-in original bytes and Rust USD/ZIP writers, without Maya,
Python, network access or native converter dependencies.

## Original exporter layer

`usda-maya-nurbs-circles.usda` is the original
`test/testSamples/basisCurves/nurbsCircleExport.usda` from
[Autodesk Maya USD at commit 48eae123cabec8e671f0779b03c22fa30631a781](https://github.com/Autodesk/maya-usd/blob/48eae123cabec8e671f0779b03c22fa30631a781/test/testSamples/basisCurves/nurbsCircleExport.usda),
renamed only for the corpus. It contains two periodic order-4 NURBS curves,
each with 11 control points, 15 knots and parameter range `(0, 8)`. Weights
are absent, so both curves use unit weights. The second curve has a `+3 Z`
placement. The upstream `testExportedNURBS` test independently identifies
this layer as exported NURBS output.

| Retained resource | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `usda-maya-nurbs-circles.usda` | 1,638 | `17b9eab67f027d314e4de32cd01d1c383068768d8b9a49c7a72ea5abc0b6057b` |
| `MAYA-USD-LICENSE.md` | 10,850 | `8173d5c29b4f956d532781d2b86e4e30f83e6b7878dce18c919451d6ba707c90` |

The complete original license and [source-attribution record](MAYA-USD-NOTICE.txt)
accompany the model. Preview PNGs are generated renderings of this separately
licensed asset, rather than MIT-authored model assets.

Catwalk's current USD reader preserves numeric coordinates and normalizes the
up axis; it does not apply `metersPerUnit`. The original `0.01` metadata is
retained, while the centerlines are approximately unit radius with `Z = 0`
and `Z = 3`. Source `widths` and the width-expanded authored `extent` are not
used to generate ribbon or tube geometry. Centerline sampling uses 24 intervals
per nonempty knot span, so the two eight-span curves produce 384 segments.

## Authored geometry controls

| Input | Literal geometry and purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `usda-nurbs-rational-weights.usda` | Three quadratic controls with the same radius-2 quarter-circle control polygon and positive, zero-middle or signed-middle weights. The positive weights describe a true circular arc; the other controls visibly distinguish rational evaluation from an unweighted spline or preweighted positions. |
| `usda-nurbs-trimmed-discontinuous.usda` | One batch of orders 2, 3 and 4 with nonuniform knots and separately trimmed ranges; another order-3 curve has a full-multiplicity interior knot and two disconnected quadratic pieces. Its gap must remain open. |
| `usda-nurbs-placed-instances.usda` | A rotated/scaled directly placed rational arc and two point instances with prototype-local, parent and per-instance transforms. Prototype geometry is not emitted as an additional visible copy. |
| `usda-nurbs-family.usda` | A combined stage with rational controls, trimmed/disconnected controls and placed instances in separate spatial groups. |
| `usdc-nurbs-family.usdc` | The same authored stage exported through the Rust USD writer as a genuine `PXR-USDC` binary crate. |
| `usd-nurbs-family.usd` | The exact binary crate bytes with the generic `.usd` extension. |
| `usdz-nurbs-family.usdz` | The same binary stage as the first and only member of a stored ZIP package, with its payload aligned to 64 bytes. |

All authored layers use Z-up numeric coordinates and `metersPerUnit = 1`.
The rational control polygon is `(2,0,0), (2,2,0), (0,2,0)` before each
diagnostic's offset. Positive weights are `(1, 1/sqrt(2), 1)`; zero-middle
weights are `(1, 0, 1)`; signed-middle weights are `(1, -0.25, 1)`, whose
homogeneous denominator remains positive over the whole authored range.
At parameter `0.5`, the three controls pass through `(sqrt(2),sqrt(2),0)`,
`(4,1,0)` and `(6+2/3,2/3,0)`, respectively. Positions in the files are
unweighted; the weights are applied during curve evaluation.

The standalone controls produce 72, 168 and 72 segments under the fixed
24-interval policy; the combined stage produces 312 segments. The four family
encodings are designed to produce identical geometry, segment order and PNGs.
Independent tests verify the sampled coordinates, knot-boundary gaps,
transforms and original source hashes; image snapshots qualify the visible
shape separately from those geometry assertions.

The schema is described by the primary
[OpenUSD NURBS curve documentation](https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_geom_nurbs_curves.html).
These cases qualify sampled curve centerlines, not NURBS patches, width-based
ribbons/tubes, motion blur or universal USD/Maya exporter compatibility.

The importer evaluates each trimmed knot span separately, retaining one-sided
values at repeated-knot boundaries. It handles orders 1–64, treats absent
weights as one, and accepts finite positive, negative, zero and mixed weights.
Constant spans become points. For weights without a strict common sign, exact
rational polynomials derived from the original binary attribute scalars cancel
factors shared by all four homogeneous components. A Sturm sequence then
certifies that the reduced denominator has no root anywhere on the closed
trimmed span, including even roots between thumbnail samples. Removable
endpoint and interior zeros retain their finite limits. Genuine poles and
identically zero denominators fail explicitly. Schema-valid ranges beyond the
active spline domain remain unsupported and fail explicitly.

Independent inline controls additionally check an interior common factor,
a factor shared by only one coordinate, a removable even root yielding a
constant point, a strictly positive denominator minimum of `2^-41`, and a
trimmed range excluding an off-grid even pole. Boundary tests check the accepted
order limit and aggregate work accounting across separately authored prims.
Further numeric controls require exact fallback for overflowing knot widths and
zero/subnormal homogeneous products, retaining original float32 endpoints under
large world placements instead of amplifying lost intermediate precision.
Normalized parameter controls retain every quadratic Bernstein sample in one-
and 25-ULP-wide knot intervals. Extreme parameter ratios and their complements
retain independently expected scaled line traces. Exactly coincident controls
produce one point with unequal positive or negative weights, while a separately
authored small rational trace remains curved without a collapse tolerance.
Stage-wide limits also bound spans, samples, output, exact operations, temporary
integer sizes and cumulative allocations, including point-instancer prototypes;
the [format coverage documentation](../../../../docs/format-coverage.md#usd)
lists these budgets.
